answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with identity-bound stake under delayed, non-transferable vesting. A newcomer must post a bond locked for a fixed horizon, withdrawable only after a cooling period, so the ledger keeps a mirror of real, unrecoverable cost per identity. Forging ten thousand puppets buys ten thousand separate sacrifices; no velvet shortcut lets one owner pool risk across aliases, each bond sits on its own vine. The attacker pays the whole sum up front, forfeits any misbehaving clone, and keeps capital idle, so swarm cost scales linearly while an honest agent amortizes one bond.
